sites.evidence_type: published tolerance of a different insertion (transposon, FP fusion)
sites.functional_impact_measured: Live-cell labeling with tetrazine-cy5 confirmed surface accessibility of the BCNK at H684; anti-myc counterstaining confirmed APP expression. APP trafficking to the cell surface was intact. Secretase processing or Aβ production was NOT MEASURED.
sites.rationale: L4 (and corroborated by L5–L9) names H609 in APP695 as the amber-suppression site. APP695 lacks the 75-residue KPI+OX2 insert present in APP770 (residues 290–364 of APP770); therefore H609(APP695) maps to H684 in the APP770 canonical sequence, confirmed by Python lookup (seq[683]='H'). Position 684 is within the extracellular domain (18–700), 17 residues from the TM boundary (701), satisfying the ≥3-residue clearance rule. Live tetrazine-cy5 labeling (L8/L9) directly demonstrates that the modification at this position is accessible from the extracellular face, making it a validated surface site. The insert_after_residue is set to 683 because the BCNK occupies position 684 (replacing H684), so an epitope tag would be placed between V683 and H684. Full-length APP695 (APP770 canonical) bearing an amber stop codon at H609 (APP695 numbering; H684 in APP770 canonical numbering) was co-expressed with PylRS-AF and Pyl-tRNA_CUA in HEK293 cells in the presence of BCNK (bicyclononyne-lysine), incorporating the non-canonical amino acid at H684 within the extracellular Aβ segment. The construct also carries a C-terminal EGFP fusion (intracellular) and a myc tag for expression verification.

sources.claim: (b) APP(H609TAG)‐EGFP expression via genetic code expansion.

literature_notes: L1 (HiBiT-tagged APP695): The ledger clip states the protein was 'tagged with the small HiBiT tag' but gives no position. HiBiT is used both N-terminally (extracellular after SP cleavage) and C-terminally (intracellular for APP) in the literature; without a stated position the site cannot be pinned and the clip is disqualified per the rules (commercial/research construct with unstated tag position). L2/L3 (Aβ segment, no residue): These clips name only the 'Aβ segment' without a specific residue; they are superseded by L4/L5 which name H609 explicitly. L6/L7 corroborate L4/L5 (same construct, same cells). L8/L9 provide the surface-accessibility validation for the H609/H684 site. The C-terminal EGFP fusion in APP(H609TAG)-EGFP is intracellular (C-terminus at residue 770, within the intracellular domain 722–770) and is recorded in other_positions.

literature_other_positions.note: APP(H609TAG)-EGFP carries EGFP fused at the C-terminus (residue 770); the C-terminus of APP is intracellular (domain 722–770), so this EGFP fusion is cytoplasmic, not a surface tag.
